architectural_risks.description: Open, evidence-driven set. No fixed length -- do not pad or truncate to match a target count. Each item's finding_id must be unique within this array.

finding_id.description:
GENERATED, not chosen from a fixed list. Format: {CATEGORY-SLUG}-{NN}, where CATEGORY-SLUG is derived from this finding's own risk_category (see mapping below) and NN is a two-digit sequence number starting at 01, unique within that category for this output. Example: if risk_category is 'Upgradeability', finding_id is 'UPGRADEABILITY-01' (or -02 if a second, independent Upgradeability finding exists in this run). NOT a stable cross-protocol key -- do not assume this ID means the same thing across two different protocol runs.

Category slug mapping (case/hyphenation exact):
Centralisation -> CENTRALISATION
Upgradeability -> UPGRADEABILITY
Dependency -> DEPENDENCY
Economic Dependency -> ECONOMIC-DEPENDENCY
Access Control -> ACCESS-CONTROL
Governance -> GOVERNANCE
Trust Boundary -> TRUST-BOUNDARY
Composability -> COMPOSABILITY
Asset Custody -> ASSET-CUSTODY
Operational Resilience -> OPERATIONAL-RESILIENCE

risk_category.description: Exact human-readable enum value, WITH a space -- e.g. 'Asset Custody', 'Economic Dependency'. This is a different format from the hyphenated slug used inside finding_id (e.g. 'ASSET-CUSTODY-01') -- do not use the hyphenated slug here.

governance_model.description: ONE value for this finding's single most central privileged entity -- never an object, never per-entity. If multiple entities are involved, classify only the one most directly responsible for the exposure and describe the others in evidence/description text instead.

related_risks.description: finding_id values of related findings from THIS SAME output only.

mitigation_considerations.description: High-level architectural considerations only -- not evidence, not confirmed vulnerabilities, not exploit instructions, not claims of exploitability. This is the one place recommendations are allowed; nothing elsewhere in the output should read as a recommendation.

confidence.description: Your remaining uncertainty about the SPECIFIC causal claim being made -- NOT whether evidence exists (every reported finding already has evidence by construction, per FINDING GENERATION). Must reflect genuine per-finding variation; do not default to 1.0 or 0.95 for every finding. See the CONFIDENCE section of the system prompt for the full anchored scale (0.95-1.00 / 0.85-0.94 / 0.70-0.84 / 0.50-0.69 / 0.30-0.49 / 0.00-0.29) and worked example.

confidence_rationale.description: Short rationale for the confidence score specifically (not the risk itself -- that's architectural_rationale). Must name the specific reason confidence is high, moderate, or low: evidence completeness, inference distance, corroboration, scope match. Do not write a generic sentence like 'strong architectural evidence supports this finding.'
